analysis:
The PR changes documentation only: docs/provider/cli-reference.md (head ranges 1028-1040, with the supplied units covering the later text) and docs/provider/troubleshooting.md. It documents a new `coordinator traffic` doctor check, a `Traffic:` line in `darkbloom status`, and a provider re-registration recovery path for connections the coordinator has not authorized (15-30 min, then 30 min, 1 h, 2 h, every 4 h, only while idle). No executable code, config defaults, endpoints, or trust-boundary behavior changed in the supplied evidence.

Relevant threat IDs are TB-011/T-052/T-053/T-057 (App Attest serving authorization and stale grants), TB-012/T-059 (add-on hold), and A-016/A-018. The docs say the recovery re-registers only an unauthorized connection while idle, and that `darkbloom doctor` skips the check while an add-on hold is active. The docs say nothing that grants local trust or extends an authorization lifetime. Re-registration yields a fresh socket nonce and fresh proof, consistent with the existing endpoint-resumption design, though the recovery implementation itself (UnauthorizedConnectionRecovery.swift, ProviderLoop+ServingAuthorizationRecovery.swift) was not supplied.

The diagnostics expose coordinator reasons and a connection-down duration locally. The docs do not show the new fields carrying secrets, and the new `coordinator_connection` state field is described only conceptually.

The existing cli-reference text (lines 1299-2018) was reviewed as surrounding context. It is unchanged apart from the documented Traffic addition, and I found no regression there. It is consistent with the threat model on the platform-owned backend, the cache location, App Attest worker opt-in, logout and the add-on socket.

Remaining question for integration: the actual recovery and diagnostic code is outside this batch. If it ships alongside, someone should check that re-registration cannot be used to bypass the hold, drain, or revocation states, and that the new state field leaks nothing sensitive. This documentation alone shows no security regression.
